fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. David says it plainly: "From the ends of the earth I call out to You whenever my heart is faint." He calls out when his heart is faint, and he says so out loud. That's the part I love.

That's it, baker. David prays, "Lead me to the rock that is higher than I." Think about that one. He's not saying he'll climb up there on his own. He asks to be LED, and I can relate, because I couldn't get out of that junk drawer by myself either.

Home is a fine thought, friend, but a father's house isn't in this psalm. David asks, "Lead me to the rock that is higher than I." He's asking for a rock that's higher than he is, not a trip back to a house. And again, he asks to be led.
Right on, baker. David says, "For You have been my refuge, a tower of strength against the enemy." Look at the words "have been." He's talking about what God has been to him, and that's a refuge.
Not this time, baker. David calls God his "…refuge, a tower of strength against the enemy." He doesn't call Him judge here. A tower of strength is a pretty good thing to have against an enemy.
Yes, baker! David prays, "Let me dwell in Your tent forever…" Not a quick stop, a forever stay. Believe me, after years stuck in the back of a junk drawer, I know a good forever when I hear one.

That one is true, friend, so we'll take the lesson and move on. Right after asking to dwell in God's tent forever, David says, "For You have heard my vows, O God…" That's exactly what the psalm says. David asks, and then he says God has heard.

Family isn't what the verse points to, baker. David says God gave him "…the inheritance reserved for those who fear Your name." The group in the verse is described by fearing God's name, not by who your father is. Family tree doesn't make the list here.
Edom isn't in this psalm, baker. The prayer for the king says, "Increase the days of the king’s life…" It's about his life stretching out, not a battle report.

That's it, baker. The prayer says, "appoint Your loving devotion and Your faithfulness to guard him." Think of those two as guards standing watch over the king. I'd take that security detail over the back of a dusty junk drawer any day.
